description.short_caption: GMS stain showing fungal elements in lung tissue.
description.detailed_description: This is a histopathology slide stained with Gomori methenamine silver (GMS), highlighting fungal elements as black or dark brown circular structures against a green background. The tissue appears to be lung parenchyma, with fungal organisms distributed throughout. The GMS stain is specific for fungal cell walls, aiding in the identification of fungal infections. No viral inclusions are visible, consistent with the negative respiratory viral panel.

description.short_caption: Axial CT of the chest showing heterogeneous consolidation in the left lung.
description.detailed_description: This axial CT image of the chest demonstrates significant heterogeneous consolidation in the left lung, with areas of air bronchograms visible. The right lung appears relatively clear. The mediastinum and heart are centrally located, and no obvious pleural effusion is seen. The image is a non-contrast study, as no enhancement is evident.
visible_findings: heterogeneous consolidation in the left lung
air bronchograms in the left lung

description.short_caption: Histopathology slide showing inflammation and necrosis (H&E stain).
description.detailed_description: This histopathology image, stained with hematoxylin and eosin (H&E), shows a region of tissue with prominent inflammatory cell infiltration, including neutrophils and other immune cells, surrounding areas of necrosis. The tissue architecture is disrupted, and there are scattered cellular debris and eosinophilic necrotic material. The background shows preserved areas of tissue with less inflammation.

description.short_caption: Graph showing the trend of urinary antigen levels over four years.
description.detailed_description: This image is a line graph depicting the trend of urinary antigen levels (ng/mL) over a four-year period. The x-axis represents time in years, while the y-axis shows urinary antigen concentration. The graph includes annotations indicating clinical events, such as symptom resolution and re-development of symptoms (e.g., shortness of breath, cough, and hypoxia). Different antifungal treatments (voriconazole, posaconazole, itraconazole, and amphotericin B) are marked with symbols along the timeline. The urinary antigen levels decrease over time, with fluctuations corresponding to clinical events and treatment changes.
visible_findings: Line graph with urinary antigen levels decreasing over time.
Annotations indicating clinical events and symptom progression.
Symbols representing antifungal treatments (voriconazole, posaconazole, itraconazole, amphotericin B).
Fluctuations in antigen levels corresponding to clinical events.

description.short_caption: Axial chest CT showing bilateral pulmonary infiltrates.
description.detailed_description: This axial CT image of the chest demonstrates bilateral pulmonary infiltrates, with areas of ground-glass opacities and consolidation. The heart and mediastinal structures appear centrally located, and no significant pleural effusion is visible. The findings suggest a possible infectious or inflammatory process in the lungs.

description.short_caption: Axial chest CT showing bilateral lung abnormalities.
description.detailed_description: This axial CT image of the chest demonstrates bilateral lung abnormalities, including areas of consolidation and ground-glass opacities. The findings are more pronounced in the lower lobes. The mediastinum appears central, and no significant pleural effusion is visible. The image is likely taken prior to a VATS-guided biopsy, as suggested by the case context.

Case_25002/figure8.jpg.source_caption: Alveolar spaces are filled with proteinaceous material consistent with alveolar proteinosis.

description.short_caption: Histopathology of lung showing alveolar spaces filled with proteinaceous material.
description.detailed_description: This histopathology image shows alveolar spaces filled with eosinophilic, proteinaceous material, consistent with alveolar proteinosis. The alveolar walls are thin and lined by flattened pneumocytes. Scattered inflammatory cells are visible within the interstitium. The staining technique appears to be hematoxylin and eosin (H&E), highlighting the proteinaceous material in pink and cellular components in purple.
visible_findings: alveolar spaces filled with eosinophilic material

description.short_caption: Axial CT of the chest showing cavitary lesions and consolidation in the lungs.
description.detailed_description: This axial CT image of the chest demonstrates bilateral lung abnormalities. The left lung shows a large cavitary lesion with surrounding consolidation, while the right lung exhibits patchy areas of ground-glass opacities and consolidation. The mediastinum appears midline, and no significant pleural effusion is visible. The findings are consistent with chronic infectious or inflammatory processes, potentially tuberculosis or fungal infection.
visible_findings: cavitary lesion in the left lung
patchy ground-glass opacities in the right lung

description.short_caption: Axial chest CT showing bilateral lung abnormalities.
description.detailed_description: This axial chest CT image demonstrates significant abnormalities in both lungs. The left lung shows extensive areas of consolidation and ground-glass opacities, consistent with an infectious or inflammatory process. The right lung also shows patchy ground-glass opacities, though less extensive than the left. The heart and mediastinal structures appear centrally located, and no obvious pleural effusion is visible. The scan is likely performed without contrast.

Case_25002/figure9.jpg.source_caption: Alveolar spaces are filled with proteinaceous material consistent with alveolar proteinosis.

description.short_caption: Histopathology showing alveolar spaces filled with proteinaceous material, consistent with alveolar proteinosis.
description.detailed_description: This histopathology image demonstrates alveolar spaces filled with eosinophilic, proteinaceous material. The alveolar walls are thin and intact, with no significant inflammatory infiltrate visible. The pink staining suggests the use of hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) stain. The findings are consistent with pulmonary alveolar proteinosis, a condition characterized by the accumulation of surfactant-like material within the alveoli.
visible_findings: eosinophilic proteinaceous material filling alveolar spaces
